items.title: Strategic Priority - Equitable Services and Opportunities
CSD-HOU-24-009, Rent Framework for Waterloo Region Housing Community Spaces
notes:
Kelly-Anne Salerno, Assistant Director Housing Operations & Administration, provided an overview of the proposed rent framework for the Waterloo Region Housing community spaces. She highlighted that the framework will establish greater transparency and sustainability as it will assist in the strengthening and expanding partnerships to ensure both cultural and financial housing supports.

In response to the Committee, K. Salerno clarified that Appendix B illustrates the size of each community space location and that currently the organizations are not paying for rent at these locations and that the intent is to negotiate a feasible rent amount for each location. She further clarified that the rent would be reinvested by Waterloo Region Housing.

The Committee requested that Staff provide the names of the organizations for each location listed in the Rent Framework Appendix B and the approximate cost for each organization, including utilities. The Committee further requested that this information be provided directly to Council prior to consideration at the May 22, 2024 Regional Council meeting.

Responding to the Committee, K. Salerno confirmed that the six hundred housing units, referenced in the report, are specifically from the current housing units under the Waterloo Region Housing umbrella that were all identified as redevelopment projects. The six hundred housing units is not the total amount of housing units being establish throughout the Region over the next 10 years.

items.title: Strategic Priority - Equitable Services and Opportunities
PDL-ECD-24-002, Youth IMPACT Project - Region of Waterloo Investment in Youth
notes:
Alison Pearson, Manager Children & Youth Planning Table, and Jahmeeks Beckford, Play Lead, Innovation Lab (Smart Waterloo Region), provided a presentation on the Youth Impact Project. A copy of the presentation is attached to the agenda. J. Beckford highlighted that the Children and Youth Planning Table and Smart Waterloo Region have been working in collaboration on this project to ensure that this project is youth driven though schools and community organizations. He further highlighted that youth participants are working to identify meaningful projects with the community organizations that will lead to project selection and implementation. A. Pearson provided an overview of next steps and noted that June 8, 2024 is the youth project pitch event. 

Responding to the Committee, J. Beckford confirmed that the expansion of youth participation, specifically the expansion of equity-seeking youths, is vital and new approaches are being considered for future projects. 

In response to the Committee, J. Beckford confirmed that both the City of Cambridge and the Townships have been collaborators and hosted several events. He further confirmed that Staff have used various tools to interest youth participants including technological opportunities as well as tactical opportunities that would not require the use of internet.

Responding to the Committee, A. Pearson and J. Beckford explained that youth participants can be recruited through previous affiliations with community organizations, but also are recruited through event projects that create more networking opportunities. J. Beckford further explained that there is also continued recruitment of organizations throughout the Region.

Received for information.

items.title: PDL-CUL-24-006, Public Art Advisory Committee Terms of Reference Update
notes:
Julian Kingston, Director of Cultural Services, provided a brief overview of the proposed Public Art Advisory Committee (PAAC) Terms of Reference. He noted that the significant update is the addition of language on reconciliation, equity, diversity, and inclusion. He further noted that the increase of membership from eight members to ten members was to promote diversity. 

The Committee acknowledged the diligent work of PAAC to update the language of the Terms of Reference.

motions.item_title: CSD-HOU-24-009, Rent Framework for Waterloo Region Housing Community Spaces
motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to the Rent Framework for Waterloo Region Housing Community Spaces as set out in report CSD-HOU-24-009 dated May 7, 2024: Approve the Rent Framework for Waterloo Region Housing Community Spaces as detailed in Appendix A; and Authorize the Commissioner of Community Services or the Commissioner of Engineering and Environmental Services to execute Waterloo Region Housing Community Space lease agreements and any ancillary documentation, subject to the parameters of Report CSD-HOU-24-009 and also to the satisfaction of the Regional Solicitor.
motions.text_html:
That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to the Rent Framework for Waterloo Region Housing Community Spaces as set out in report CSD-HOU-24-009 dated May 7, 2024:

  1. Approve the Rent Framework for Waterloo Region Housing Community Spaces as detailed in Appendix A; and
  2. Authorize the Commissioner of Community Services or the Commissioner of Engineering and Environmental Services to execute Waterloo Region Housing Community Space lease agreements and any ancillary documentation, subject to the parameters of Report CSD-HOU-24-009 and also to the satisfaction of the Regional Solicitor.
